cards.text: Friend, we made it to the very last chapter of Isaiah. The LORD has just promised comfort for Jerusalem and said His wrath will be shown to His enemies (Isaiah 66:13-14). Now the prophet says look: the LORD will come with fire, and His chariots are like a whirlwind.

cards.question: The LORD is coming with fire, His chariots like a whirlwind. What is He coming to do?

answers.text: Carry out His anger and rebuke
Rest in a house built for Him

cards.text: Fire and a sword. The prophet says the LORD will use both to execute judgment.

cards.question: The prophet says the LORD will execute judgment by fire and by His sword on all flesh.

cards.text: Many will be slain by the LORD. Then the LORD calls out a group: people who consecrate and purify themselves to enter the groves.

They follow one in the center of those who eat swine, vermin and rats. All that purifying and then straight into the middle of the RAT eaters is like washing your car and parking it under a tree full of pigeons.

cards.question: The LORD says the people who purify themselves to enter the groves will perish together.

cards.text: Now here comes the turn. The LORD says He knows their deeds and their thoughts, and He is coming to gather.

cards.question: Who is the LORD coming to gather?
Once all nations and tongues are gathered, what will they come and see?

cards.text: The LORD says He will establish a sign among them and send survivors to the nations: Tarshish, Put, the archers of Lud, Tubal, Javan and the islands far away.
TARSHISH! That's where Jonah's ship was headed when he ran from the Lord (Jonah 1:3). This time the LORD is the one booking the trip.

cards.question: The islands far away have already heard of the LORD's fame and seen His glory.
The survivors sent out to those faraway nations will ___ the LORD's glory among them.

cards.text: The survivors are out there telling the nations about the LORD's glory. Then the LORD says they will bring all your brothers from all the nations.
They come on horses, chariots, wagons, mules AND camels. That's every ride on the lot, and here I am getting around by hopping on a gold base.

cards.question: Where are all those brothers brought from the nations?
The brothers are brought from all the nations as a ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: The LORD says it's just like the Israelites bringing an offering in a clean vessel to His house. People carried in like an offering in a clean vessel.

cards.question: The LORD says He will select some of those gathered as what?

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about the new heavens and the new earth, which He will make. They will endure before Him.

cards.question: The LORD says that just as the new heavens and the new earth will endure, "your descendants and your name will endure."
The LORD says that from one New Moon to another and one Sabbath to another, only Israel will come to worship before Him.
As the worshipers go forth, what does the LORD say they will see?

answers.text: The corpses of those who rebelled
A river flowing from the mountain

cards.question: The LORD says the fire of the men who rebelled against Him will one day be quenched.

cards.text: Their worm will never die, and they will be a horror to all mankind. That's the last verse of Isaiah, friend: the nations coming to see His glory, and a sober warning to close the book.

findings.problem: Story card 3 already tells the baker that the LORD will use fire and a sword to execute judgment. That leaves only 'on all flesh' for the true/false to test, so the earlier card gives away almost the whole answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'All that purifying and then straight into the middle of the RAT eaters' laughs at the people in the passage. It calls them 'RAT eaters' in capitals instead of finding the humor in their human situation.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: This is a 'who' question, but the wrong answers 'A few towns of Judah' and 'One family in Jerusalem' are vague inventions, not real details from the Bible. 'All nations and tongues' also sounds more like the Bible than the other two, so it stands out.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: This story card only comments on card 11 (Tarshish and Jonah). It tells no new part of Isaiah 66 and does not move the baker forward, so the joke is not riding along on a card that tells the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The first sentence ('The survivors are out there telling the nations about the LORD's glory') recaps Isaiah 66:19, but the card cites only Isaiah 66:20.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The second sentence ('People carried in like an offering in a clean vessel') just repeats the first. The card adds nothing and has no Papa Dorin voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: 'That's the last verse of Isaiah, friend: the nations coming to see His glory, and a sober warning' recaps Isaiah 66:18. It also says the last verse includes the nations seeing His glory, which it doesn't: Isaiah 66:24 is only about the corpses of the rebels. The card cites only 66:24.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The closing line works as a recap of the passage instead of telling the last verse.

Only three of the twelve story cards carry a joke (stop 1 cards 6 and 12, stop 2 card 2). Many story cards read flat, with no Papa Dorin voice, for example stop 1 cards 3, 8 and 11 and stop 2 cards 5 and 7.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation.
